[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we can start, is this time still good for everyone?

[00:18] Priya: okay cool, so for Q2 we saw a steady ramp in tokens used, roughly 38% q/q growth, embeddings are up 18% driven by the new semantic search flow. There's a spike mid-June that correlates with the customer support ticketing ingestion run. Some of that was batch embedding churn.
[00:35] Liam: yeah that June run was our big CSV import, we should have throttled it, that caused a lot of prefix cache misses.
[00:41] Marcus: right, the import also stressed the KV cache, we saw increased latencies because the cache warmup was happening on a lot of cold prefixes. We recommended a pre-warming approach in the previous notes but it looks like it wasn't applied.
[00:52] Aisha: can you briefly explain what you mean by KV cache pre-warm? Diego wasn't sure.
[00:56] Marcus: sure, so Redwood's runtime keeps a key-value cache for decoder states, when many sequentially different prompts hit the cluster cold, the runtime has to recompute caches leading to higher p95 latencies. Pre-warm is basically priming the common prompt prefixes during the ETL so the cache is hot when the bulk queries happen. (some audio glitch) I think that was in the ops doc we shared.
[01:20] Diego: ah right okay, we missed that step during the import run. We'll add pre-warm to the ingestion pipeline.
[01:25] Priya: on cost, initial analysis shows the June spike added about 14% to the monthly bill for that period, and the per-embedding unit cost is the dominant factor for that batch. We can look at batching and instead of per-row call pattern do a chunked embedding call to reduce overhead.
[01:40] Liam: what's our marginal cost if we move to dedicated? Would that bring down the per-token unit cost materially?
[01:45] Jordan: good question — yes, Dedicated reduces unit costs for sustained throughput; depends on commit level. For example, for the size you're running (your 95th percentile concurrent) our estimate shows ~30-45% unit cost improvement vs hosted passthrough for heavy embedding workloads, primarily because of reserved GPU amortization and better batching efficiency.
[02:04] Aisha: can you share those numbers in a table after the call? We need to show this to finance.
[02:08] Jordan: absolutely, I'll include a line-item comparison (hosted vs dedicated) including assumptions.
[02:13] Marcus: also worth noting, quantization and model selection matter. If you can accept slightly lower max-context for embeddings or try the new q4 variant we've been validating, you can get additional cost wins. We can run a quick eval on your sample dataset during the sizing workshop.
[02:30] Diego: any concerns about quality regression with q4?
[02:33] Marcus: usually minimal for semantic similarity, but we should validate with Arcadia's test prompts. We'll include an eval plan.
[02:40] Priya: on reliability, there were two incidents in May where we saw degraded throughput for roughly 18 minutes each. Root cause was an autoscaler misconfiguration on one of the pools that caused a delayed scale up under burst. Redwood has since applied the autoscaler threshold fix and added a fallback policy to route to a secondary region when local capacity is constrained.
[02:58] Liam: were there any data exposure concerns during that time?
[03:01] Jordan: no, those incidents were capacity related only—no logs or payloads were leaked. We do have audit logs showing normal access patterns. We'll share the incident postmortem link.
[03:10] Aisha: okay good. On the security front, we need SSO/SAML for our org and KMS integration for embedding keys, is that on your roadmap?
[03:18] Priya: yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning are GA for Redwood, and KMS for customer-key wrapping is supported in Private deployments and via KMS integrations in Dedicated — we'll send the architecture doc.
[03:29] Aisha: what's the difference if we stay hosted vs move to private for KMS?
[03:33] Marcus: hosted integrates with Redwood-managed keys by default; with Dedicated we can enable customer-managed KMS via our cloud KMS link. For fully private/on-prem we can do HSM integrations but that is a separate engagement and timeline. It's mostly about control and auditability vs speed of setup.
[03:50] Liam: timeline wise, if we want Dedicated in production, how long does provisioning take?
[03:54] Jordan: typical Dedicated onboarding is 4-8 weeks depending on compliance needs and network setup. If VPC peering and firewall rules are simple, it's on the lower end; if you need air-gapped or custom HSM it's longer.
[04:07] Diego: we have a PCI-similar compliance posture, so we'll need more audit logs retention and fine-grained RBAC. Is longer retention an add-on?
[04:14] Priya: retention is configurable, and long-term retention is an add-on offering with archive pricing. We can propose a retention plan that meets your audit window.
[04:21] Aisha: thanks. Another thing — we noticed some increased error rates on the inference path last week for a small percentage of calls. Marcus, do you have details?
[04:29] Marcus: yes, that was tied to a model version mismatch during a canary deploy. Canary routing wasn't fully aligned with the pinned model version for one route, so some requests hit a model variant with a different tokenizer config; we rolled back the canary and fixed the routing rules. We're also recommending model-version pinning in your route configs to avoid surprise tokenization diffs.
[04:49] Liam: is there a guardrail in Redwood console to prevent that?
[04:52] Jordan: there is an option to pin versions and to enforce a canary policy which can include automatic rollback if latency or error thresholds breach. We'll walk through the console settings in the follow-up workshop.
[05:01] Priya: on roadmap asks from Arcadia, I captured: stronger RBAC, longer audit retention, pilot for Dedicated capacity, and improved embedding batching docs. Anything else?
[05:10] Aisha: also better billing granularity, we want per-team cost centers so our internal chargeback works.
[05:15] Jordan: we can expose per-api-key breakdowns and integrate with your cost center tags; we'll include that in the cost export.
[05:20] Diego: quick question on throttling — if we hit a sudden spike again, what's Redwood's recommendation? Do we rely on autoscale or should we throttle client side?
[05:27] Marcus: hybrid approach, autoscale handles steady increases but for bursty flows client-side backpressure and request batching is better. We also recommend prefix caching and request coalescing for your search traffic.
[05:37] Liam: ok makes sense. For the Dedicated sizing workshop, who's the right team to include from Arcadia? We'll need devops, mlops, and finance.

We can share a short benchmarking note tailored to your workload.
